models: IRP (GPT-2 Imitator, DistilBERT Retriever, BART Paraphraser)
answer_1.outputs: expository documents (paragraphs describing the given topic)

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the quality of the generated documents with two sets of metrics. First, we use traditional metrics. ROUGE-1 (R1) and ROUGE-2 (R2), BLEU, and METEOR measure the similarity between the predicted and true outputs. ... we also adopt existing factuality metrics. First, we calculate the average percentage of tokens ... Next, we use FactCC, ... we calculate if the generated text is entailed (NLI-Ent) or contradicted (NLI-Contr) by the true output.

answer_4.quote: To further test the quality of the generated expository texts, we invite two computer science and engineering college students to evaluate 30 random expository documents in the test sets produced by each baseline on U.S. News and Medline. ... we ask annotators to evaluate on Style adherence to the true output (i.e. organization and phrasing), and Factuality on a 5-Likert scale. For Fact, we provide annotators with the true output and encourage them to use external resources (Google Search).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each generated document on Style adherence (organization and phrasing) and Factuality using a 5‑point Likert scale, optionally consulting external resources.
